newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-AUSTRIAN MEN ON FORM AFTER BREAK.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-AUSTRIAN MEN ON FORM AFTER BREAK.

text.p: The Austrian men downhillers returned on form from their brief Christmas break on Friday to put five in the fastest 10 in first training for Sunday's World Cup race.

Werner Franz, in search of victory after finishing second in the opening men's downhill of the season in Val d'Isere this month, was the fastest in two minutes 0.91 seconds down Bormio's steep and icy Stelvio piste.

He was followed by compatriot Fritz Strobl, winner in France, 0.89 seconds behind. Italian Peter Runggaldier was equal third fastest with Norwegian veteran Atle Skaardal in 2:02.30, 1.39 seconds slower than Franz.
Josef Strobl, Guenther Mader and Roland Assinger -- seventn, eighth and ninth -- were the other Austrians in the top 10.
The Austrian men dominated Val d'Isere, with the top four finishers, and also set the pace in training for the last two downhills at Val Gardena just before Christmas.
But their prowess in training vanished on race days and only Josef Strobl made the grade with a third place.
Sunday's race -- on a piste made faster by extremely low recent temperatures in the Italian resort-- could restore the Austrians to the top of the podium.
But their rivals also looked sharp.

Luc Alphand, downhill World Cup champion for the past two seasons and winner here during the 1995 World Cup finals, was fifth fastest in a time of 2:02.59 although the Frenchman rarely sets much store by his training times.
Alphand won one downhill in Val Gardena last week and came second in another without pushing himself in practice.
Italy's Kristian Ghedina, the other winner in Val Gardena, was sixth fastest in 2:02.96, right behind Alphand.
Norway's Lasse Kjus, the overall World Cup champion and winner here last December, had hoped to return this weekend from a bout of 'flu but team officials said he was not fit.
Kjetil-Andre Aamodt, Norway's other main all-rounder, is reportedly tired and decided to give Bormio a miss.
Their absence should allow current overall leader Hans Knauss of Austria to forge further ahead but his training time on Friday was far from impressive.
Knauss was 51st fastest -- or the 16th slowest -- in 2:07.01 and more than six seconds behind team mate Franz.
France's Nicolas Burtin, whose best career place to date is sixth in the 1994 Lillehammer Olympic downhill, was involved in a serious training incident when he crashed out.
Burtin, who started 64th out of 71 racers, said after immediate checks that his team doctor feared he had torn the cruciate ligaments of his right knee and fractured his tibia.
The skier, who also finished eighth in a downhill in Val Gardena in 1994 but has missed the last two seasons because of injury, was to return to France later on Friday.
